To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new readout that reduces parameters per neuron in a data-driven neural response prediction model of mouse visual cortex by up to two-orders of magnitude, and that we trained a convolutional core that generalizes to a new animal and outperforms VGG16.
a convolutional core trained on data from multiple animals can be used to generalize to new animals and that this core captures general cortical features.
we train a deep convolutional network that predicts neural population activity from natural image stimuli in primary visual cortex (area V1) of the mouse brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
generalization in data-driven deep learning models of neural population activity in primary visual cortex.
understanding the computational principles of visual processing in the mammalian cortex, and in particular the mechanisms of generalization in the cortex.
the generalization of deep learning models in data-driven models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the convolutional core captures general cortical features that can generalize across animals and that the readout is crucial for achieving this generalization.
the convolutional core of our data-driven network generalizes between animals and captures characteristic cortical features better than VGG16.

our network outperforms the previous state-of-art by 7% in performance and 2 orders of magnitude in the number of parameters in the readout and that it is the first model to generalize between animals in a transfer learning setup.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model is the first data-driven model of V1 to capture generalizable cortical features and to be able to predict neural responses from natural images.
the core of our network captures generalizing features of primary visual cortex, and the novel readout enables a data-driven model of mouse V1 that generalizes between animals and is data-efficient.

the core of a deep network is indeed a good candidate for representing general cortical features and that a linear readout can be used to predict neural responses from natural images with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the core of a DNN can indeed be trained in a data-driven way to capture general cortical features.
a core trained on data-driven features is a better starting point for transfer learning than a pre-trained task-driven network such as VGG.
a data-driven convolutional core trained on neural responses in V1 generalizes well between animals, and can thus be used to predict neural responses in a different animal without retraining.
